panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (a, b, c, d). a: Axial brain MRI of a vesicular-stage neurocysticercus with the characteristic cyst-with-dot appearance representing the scolex. [raw subtype: vesicular stage] b: Axial contrast-enhanced brain CT demonstrates a degenerating ring-enhancing cyst with surrounding perilesional edema, corresponding to the colloidal stage of neurocysticercosis. [raw subtype: colloidal stage] c: The caption explicitly identifies a neurocysticercus in the granular stage without perilesional edema. The granular-stage morphology is not represented by a dedicated finding key. [raw subtype: granular stage] d: Axial noncontrast head CT shows multiple punctate intracranial calcifications characteristic of calcified-stage neurocysticercosis. [raw subtype: calcified stage]

panels.figure_caption: (a) MRI image revealing vesicular cysticerci (the central dot represents the scolex). (b) Cyst beginning to degenerate with perilesional edema and enhancement in the colloidal stage. (c) Cyst in the granular stage without perilesional edema. (d) CAT scan revealing multiple calcifications in the calcified stage.
in_text_mentions: erilesional edema and do not enhance after administration of contrast medium. There may be a bright nodule in their interior giving the lesion a “hole with dot” appearance that represents the scolex (Figure 2(a)) [55]. As the cysts begin to degenerate they appear as ill-defined lesions surrounded by edema which enhance after contrast medium administration. This is the colloidal stage of the cyst and represents the so-called “acute encephalitic phase” of NCC which likely represents an intense host reaction to the parasite (Figure 2(b)).
